The chapter states it verbatim: "The earliest museum (6th century B.C.E.) in the world was discovered during the excavations at the city of 'Ur' in Mesopotamia. The excavations were conducted by Sir Leonard Woolley (1922-1934)." So the answer is (c) Ur.

Kolkata is the deliberate near-miss — the chapter does say the 'Indian Museum' at Kolkata was founded by the Asiatic Society in 1814 C.E., but that museum was founded, not discovered in an excavation, and 1814 C.E. is far later than the 6th century B.C.E. Harappa is not linked to any museum in this chapter, and the chapter's only Delhi claim is about the National Archives, which is an archive rather than a museum.

The chapter states it in a single sentence: "The National Archives of India is in New Delhi. Every state in India maintains its archives independently." So the answer is (a) New Delhi.

The chapter associates Kolkata with the Indian Museum, not the National Archives, and never mentions Mumbai or Chennai in connection with any archive. Note the nearby distractor fact the chapter does give — the main office of the National Film Archives of India is in Pune — which is a different institution, and Pune is not among the options.
